To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students in this sixth grade urban class used their knowledge of rap and theater to develop a genre that was used in their science class.
the students' knowledge building emerged as an interactive social process, and that students' affective engagement was a key aspect of their knowledge building.

students' work (plays and songs) in an urban science classroom revealed that students' affective responses were integral to their developing scientific knowledge, that students' knowledge building was a social process involving transactions between and among students, that the classroom genre that emerged from students' work was different from that which the teacher sought to establish in her classroom, and that gender was related to the way that students' included disagreement in their classroom genre.
In summary, our research is concerned with
students' science learning and knowledge building as a social activity.
the ways students' affective responses and their social interactions are intertwined with the development of their scientific understanding.

the nature of the learning that is possible in a science classroom where students and teachers are actively engaged in the construction of knowledge, and where the students are actively involved in constructing their own classroom community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study has shown that students' work in science is not only about science.
the students' knowledge construction is a social and affective process.

the students in this class did indeed construct knowledge, but it was a knowledge construction that was very much influenced by the students' own affective and social reactions to the classroom situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students' work revealed a complex interplay of affect, cognition, and social processes.
students' work in science is an expression of a range of transactions between students, between students and the teacher, and among the students and the teacher.

the affective and the social aspects of students' learning are intertwined with their cognition and that the social and affective aspects of learning science are important to understand in their own right.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we must attend to students' affective responses to science and their social interactions as we seek to help them learn science.
the affective aspects of science learning are an important part of the learning process and cannot be ignored if we are to understand how students learn.
students' work in science classrooms can be understood in terms of the ways genres brought by students and teachers meet in the classroom.
